'''Wendy Anne Bickmore''' (born 28 July 1961)<ref name=whoswho>{{Who's Who|title=Bickmore, Prof. Wendy Anne|year=2022|id=U274935|doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U274935}}</ref> is a British [[genomics|genome biologist]] known for her research on the organisation of genomic material in cells.

==Early life and education==
Bickmore was born at [[Shoreham-by-Sea]] on 28 July 1961 to Beryl and Keith Bickmore.<ref name=whoswho/> She was educated at [[Chichester High School for Girls]]<ref name=whoswho/> where her interest in science began being influenced by her biology teacher and her parents who were keen amateur gardeners. Her interest in biochemistry was confirmed having read 'The Chemistry of Life' by [[Steven Rose]]<ref>{{Cite book |last=Rose, Steven P. R. (Steven Peter Russell), 1938- |title=The chemistry of life. |date=1979 |publisher=Penguin |others=Sanderson, Cath |isbn=0-14-020790-2 |edition=2nd |location=Harmondsworth |oclc=6426479}}</ref> and she went on to study biochemistry at [[St Hugh's College, Oxford]]<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.st-hughs.ox.ac.uk/wp-content/uploads/St-Hughs-Chronicle-2015-2016.pdf|title=St Hugh's College Chronicle 2015–16|year=2016|publisher=St Hugh's College, Oxford|page=41}}</ref> graduating with a BA. She then undertook a PhD at the [[University of Edinburgh]] analysing [[nucleic acid sequence]]s from the [[Y chromosome]] of humans.<ref>{{Cite thesis |title=Molecular analysis of DNA sequences from the human Y chromosome |date=1986 |language=English |first=Wendy Anne |last=Bickmore |oclc=606140886}}</ref> Her supervisors were Howard Cooke<ref name="phd">{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Edinburgh|title=Molecular analysis of DNA sequences from the human Y chromosome|first= Wendy Anne|last=Bickmore|year=1986|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.375478|oclc=499825888}}|hdl=1842/10808}} {{free access}}</ref> and [[Adrian Bird]].<ref name=bird>{{Cite book|series=Methods in Enzymology|year=1992|volume=216|title=Recombinant DNA Part G|last1=Bickmore|first1=Wendy A.|last2=Bird|first2=Adrian P.|chapter=Use of restriction endonucleases to detect and isolate genes from mammalian cells |pages=[https://archive.org/details/recombinantdna0000unse/page/224 224–244]|language=en|doi=10.1016/0076-6879(92)16024-e|pmid=1336093|isbn=978-0-12-182117-3|chapter-url=https://archive.org/details/recombinantdna0000unse/page/224}}</ref> She was an independent fellow at the [[Lister Institute of Preventive Medicine]] from 1991 until 1996.<ref name=":1" />

==Research and career==
Her work has focused on how [[DNA]], [[chromosome]]s and specific [[gene]]s are organised and packaged in the [[cell nucleus]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thenakedscientists.com/HTML/interviews/interview/1000180/|publisher=thenakedscientists.com|title=Prof Wendy Bickmore – Packing DNA|date=4 August 2013 }}</ref> how this process is regulated during development to facilitate the expression of genes, and how aberrant genome organisation is linked to disease.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hgu.mrc.ac.uk/people/w.bickmore.html |title=wendy bickmore |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090403164354/http://www.hgu.mrc.ac.uk/people/w.bickmore.html |archive-date=2009-04-03 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Pritchard-Jones|first1=Kathryn|last2=Fleming|first2=Stewart|last3=Davidson|first3=Duncan|last4=Bickmore|first4=Wendy|last5=Porteous|first5=David|last6=Gosden|first6=Christine|last7=Bard|first7=Jonathan|last8=Buckler|first8=Alan|last9=Pelletier|first9=Jerry|s2cid=4350729|year=1990|title=The candidate Wilms' tumour gene is involved in genitourinary development|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=346|issue=6280|pages=194–197|doi=10.1038/346194a0|pmid=2164159|bibcode=1990Natur.346..194P}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Croft|first1=Jenny A.|last2=Bridger|first2=Joanna M.|last3=Boyle|first3=Shelagh|last4=Perry|first4=Paul|last5=Teague|first5=Peter|last6=Bickmore|first6=Wendy A.|year=1999|title=Differences in the Localization and Morphology of Chromosomes in the Human Nucleus|journal=[[Journal of Cell Biology]]|language=en|volume=145|issue=6|pages=1119–1131|doi=10.1083/jcb.145.6.1119|issn=0021-9525|pmid=10366586|pmc=2133153}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fraser|first1=Peter|last2=Bickmore|first2=Wendy|s2cid=4388060|title=Nuclear organization of the genome and the potential for gene regulation|year=2007|journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|volume=447|issue=7143|pages=413–417|doi=10.1038/nature05916|pmid=17522674|bibcode=2007Natur.447..413F}}</ref>

In 2020, she was recognised for her research examining the likelihood that people will develop serious symptoms of the [[COVID-19]] disease.<ref>{{Cite web|title=New Year Honours: who from Herefordshire has been recognised?|url=https://www.herefordtimes.com/news/18977379.new-year-honours-herefordshire-recognised/|access-date=2021-11-28|website=Hereford Times|date=30 December 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

Bickmore was president of [[The Genetics Society]] from 2015 until 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|title=History|url=https://genetics.org.uk/mission-and-priorities-2/history/|access-date=2021-11-28|website=Genetics Society|language=en-GB}}</ref>

As of 2021, she is director of the [[MRC Human Genetics Unit]] at the [[University of Edinburgh]].<ref name="orcid">Wendy Bickmore {{ORCID|0000-0001-6660-7735}}</ref><ref name=":1">Wendy Bickmore {{Cite web|title=Wendy Bickmore website|date=15 January 2018 |access-date=November 28, 2021|url=https://www.ed.ac.uk/mrc-human-genetics-unit/research/bickmore-group}}</ref>

She is a member of the editorial board for ''[[Genes & Development]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://genesdev.cshlp.org/site/misc/edboard.xhtml|title=Genes & Development -- Genes & Development Editorial Board|website=genesdev.cshlp.org|access-date=2019-04-28}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Bickmore was awarded [[EMBO Membership]] in 2001,<ref name=membo>{{cite web|url=http://people.embo.org/profile/wendy-bickmore|website=people.embo.org|title=EMBO member: Wendy Bickmore|location=Heidelberg|author=Anon|year=2001}}</ref> elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh]] (FRSE) in 2005<ref name=whoswho/> and elected a [[Fellow of the Academy of Medical Sciences]] in 2005 (FMedSci).<ref name=fmedsci>{{cite web|url=http://www.acmedsci.ac.uk/fellows/fellows-directory/ordinary-fellows/professor-wendy-bickmore/|website=acmedsci.ac.uk|title=Professor Wendy Bickmore FRS FRSE FMedSci|access-date=17 September 2015|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304074831/http://www.acmedsci.ac.uk/fellows/fellows-directory/ordinary-fellows/professor-wendy-bickmore/}}</ref> She was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2017|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2017]].<ref name=frs>{{cite web|author=Anon|year=2017|title=Wendy Bickmore FRS|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/wendy-bickmore-13380/|publisher=royalsociety.org|location=London}}</ref> She was appointed [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the [[2021 New Year Honours]] for services to biomedical sciences and women in science.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=63218|supp=y|page=N8|date=31 December 2020}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
She is a member of the organisation [[Trees for Life (Scotland)|Trees for Life]] which is working to restore the forest in the Highlands of [[Scotland]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Wimmer|first=Doris|title=Wendy Bickmore|url=https://2020.eshg.org/index.php/eshg-award/|access-date=2021-11-28|website=ESHG Conference 2020|language=en-GB}}</ref>
